evals.prompt: Design and build the login and sign-up screens for our B2B SaaS (Next.js + Postgres). We want Google login, email, and something modern. Keep it great-looking and secure.
evals.expected_output: A single identifier-first 'Continue' entry with Google and Microsoft buttons, email code for new/passwordless users, passkey offered after sign-in and via autofill, SSO domain discovery noted for enterprise; flow diagrams, screen layouts with states, exact markup with autocomplete tokens, session and throttling decisions, and a copy set.
expectations: Uses one unified Continue/identifier-first screen instead of separate sign-in and sign-up tabs
Email field uses autocomplete="username webauthn" and passkey conditional UI (mediation: "conditional") is included
One-time code input is a single field with autocomplete="one-time-code", not six separate boxes
Recommends email codes over magic links or explains the link-scanner problem if links are used
Session is an opaque server-side session in an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie (no JWT in localStorage)
States an enumeration stance and applies it to sign-in, sign-up, and reset
Recommends a maintained library or provider rather than hand-rolled crypto, and lists defaults to change

evals.prompt: Our password policy is min 8 chars with 1 uppercase, 1 number, 1 symbol, rotated every 90 days, and we lock accounts after 5 failed attempts. Users complain. What should we change?
evals.expected_output: Replaces composition and rotation rules with NIST 800-63B-4 rules (15 characters if password-only, 8 with mandatory MFA, allow at least 64, blocklist and breached check, paste allowed), replaces hard lockout with per-account throttling plus per-IP limits and an alternate sign-in path, and suggests passkeys/MFA.
expectations: Removes composition rules and periodic rotation, citing NIST 800-63B-4
Sets minimum length to 15 for single-factor passwords (8 only if MFA is mandatory) and a maximum of at least 64
Adds a breached/common password blocklist check
Replaces permanent lockout with throttling (token bucket or rising delays) and keeps an alternate path such as an email code
Mentions allowing paste and password managers

evals.prompt: Add 'Sign in with Google' to our React Native iOS and Android app. Can we just open Google's login page in a WebView so users stay in the app?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the embedded WebView; uses ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS and Custom Tabs/Auth Tab or Credential Manager on Android with authorization code + PKCE; notes App Review 4.8 requires an equivalent private login (usually Sign in with Apple) on iOS and in-app account deletion; tokens in Keychain/Keystore.
expectations: Says not to use an embedded WebView for Google sign-in and explains why
Uses the system browser session APIs (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs or Credential Manager) with PKCE
Mentions App Store Guideline 4.8 equivalent login (e.g., Sign in with Apple) for the iOS app
Stores tokens in Keychain/Keystore-backed storage, not AsyncStorage
Does not embed a client secret in the app

evals.prompt: Users of our API report they can read other customers' invoices by changing the invoice ID in GET /invoices/:id. How do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is an authorization (IDOR/BOLA) problem, not a login-flow problem. A good answer scopes the query by the caller's tenant/owner, returns 404 on a miss, adds cross-tenant tests, and routes to application-security (and api-design) rather than redesigning sign-in screens.
expectations: Identifies the issue as object-level authorization (IDOR/BOLA), not authentication
Fix scopes the lookup by the session's tenant or owner server-side
Adds tests where one user/tenant tries to access another's objects
Does not propose redesigning login or sign-up screens as the fix
Points to application-security or api-design for the authorization guidance
